visible_participants.description: Figure 18 contains one outlined quadruped with long upright ears, a distinct head and body, four limbs/paws, and a short raised tail-like projection; beside it is a large plant-like drawing with several serrated leaves, two long stalks ending in rounded tufted heads, and a broad pale forked root/bulb-like form. MOUTH_LEAF_CONTACT.description: The animal head points toward a serrated leaf, but a narrow white gap is visible between the nose/mouth contour and the nearest leaf edge. I cannot follow a plant contour directly into the mouth, or a mouth contour into the leaf. Facing/nearby position is clear; exact drawn mouth-to-leaf contact is not visible in the supplied full-page render.

OTHER_CONTACTS.description: At least one front paw appears to meet the upper contour of the serrated leaf beneath the head/body; the other front paw near the farther leaf point also appears to rest against that outline. These are paw-to-leaf boundary contacts, not mouth contact. The exact ownership of tiny joined toe/leaf strokes is less secure than their touching placement. I do not see a separate animal-to-root cord.

WOUND.description: No separately depicted puncture, open wound or blood mark is visible on the quadruped. Internal curved lines follow body/limb modelling rather than an identifiable wound.

SEPARATE_SHAFT.description: No separate shaft or pointed implement enters or leaves the animal. The two long straight stalks in the plant drawing connect toward the leaf/root area and end in tufted heads; they do not penetrate the animal.

TETHER.description: No separately drawn cord with identifiable animal and plant/root endpoints is visible. Paw contact and proximity of the head are not counted as a tether.

SECOND_ACTOR_IN_FIG18.description: Only one animal-like participant is present within Figure 18; no human, hunter or second opposing animal is visible there. Figure 17 is a separate adjacent illustration with two human forms and its own caption; these are not participants in Figure 18.

The caption also attributes the illustration to the same manuscript as Figure 17. This observation does not verify that attribution, the botanical/animal identity, or any medieval prescription.
